clue.text: Physicist's short course in computer knowledge just beginning

indicators.note: in places the shortened course inside the letters for the computer

parts.note: PC, a personal computer

indicators.note: short tells you the word for course loses its final letter

parts.note: a lane is a course, as on a running track or in a swimming pool

indicators.note: just beginning means only the opening letter of knowledge is used

explanation.surface: A scientist is taking a brief class in IT that has only recently started.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'short course' is not a brief class but a track clipped by 'short'; 'in' and 'just beginning' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Planck was the German scientist who founded quantum theory; the possessive is read as 'physicist is'.

clue.text: Guerrilla leader films drug dealers

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary of the Cuban campaign
as a verb: a window films over, or mists, with condensation

explanation.surface: A rebel commander is secretly recording narcotics pushers on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests criminals selling narcotics, but the dealers are high-street pharmacists, and 'films' is a verb about glass clouding over. In Britain a chemist is a pharmacist.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful description: British pharmacists dispense and sell medicines, so they deal in drugs quite legally.

clue.text: Supply with food like grapefruit, wanting different starter?

indicators.note: the word needs a new opening letter in place of its own, with a pun on the first course of a meal

parts.note: grapefruit tastes rather sour, so it is sourish

explanation.surface: A diner is offered something citrus but would rather begin the meal with another dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting different starter' swaps the first letter of SOURISH, S, for N; the clue does not say which letter comes in, so the definition settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to feed someone is to give them the sustenance they need.

clue.text: Learner still worried about that first gear?

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate in Britain

indicators.note: about places the word for worried around the word for still

parts.note: something that worried you ate at you
yet means still, as in 'there is yet time'

explanation.surface: A novice driver remains anxious about engaging the lowest gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The gear is not in a car's gearbox: it is kit, here the first clothes a newborn wears. 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: it is the set of clothing and bedding prepared for a newborn baby, their earliest kit.

clue.text: Opponent cannot win, being regularly eliminated

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is struck out, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A rival has no hope of victory, since they keep getting knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being regularly eliminated' strikes out every other letter of 'cannot win', leaving the second, fourth, sixth and eighth.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a person who is against something, such as a protester.

clue.text: Lack of harmony is issue in part of ballet

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the word for part of ballet

parts.note: a dance is one number within a ballet
taken as written
issue means offspring, and a son is one example

explanation.surface: Discord is the trouble in one section of a ballet production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is not a problem here but offspring, and the first 'is' is simply spelt out; the 'in' after issue is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: discord, whether between musical notes or between people.

clue.text: Chinese army loses dominance in central parts of orient

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: in places the word for loses dominance inside the pair of letters taken from orient
central parts of picks the two letters at the heart of orient

parts.note: a power that wanes is losing its dominance

explanation.surface: Beijing's forces are losing their grip on the heartlands of the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The army is the Territorial Army, Britain's old volunteer reserve, not China's; 'in' and 'central parts of' work on orient.
explanation.definitionFit: An example by ethnicity and language: most people of that island are of Han descent and speak Mandarin.

clue.text: About start of season, top side almost lost

parts.note: A is the top grade or class

indicators.note: About places the top-side letters around the single letter from season
almost tells you the word for side loses its final letter

parts.note: a side in sport is a team

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of season

explanation.surface: Early in the campaign, the league leaders were nearly beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' is not a defeat but bewilderment. 'almost' shortens the side, 'About' wraps the result round the letter 'start of' picks.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone baffled and confused is said to be all adrift like this.

clue.text: Suffering cuts, college illogically put back subject

indicators.note: put back means that run of letters is read from right to left
the two words suffer cuts at each side, trimming them down to a run of letters across their join

explanation.surface: Hit by budget reductions, a college unreasonably reinstated a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering cuts' trims 'college illogically' down to EGEIL, and 'put back' turns that round. The subject is not an academic course but a vassal.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal usage the word can mean a vassal owing allegiance to a lord, as well as the lord himself.

clue.text: Restaurant, say, cut cheese sandwiches

indicators.note: the cheese sandwiches the other piece, so it goes around the outside of it

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: cut tells you the word for say loses its final letter

parts.note: to say something firmly is to assert it

explanation.surface: A cafe has, for instance, sliced-cheese sandwiches on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is not 'for example' but a verb to be shortened by 'cut', and 'sandwiches' is a verb telling the cheese to go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an informal French-style eating place serving meals and drinks.

clue.text: A grand I collected must include money for financial assistance

indicators.note: must include says the rearranged letters take the word for money inside them
collected suggests the letters are gathered up and put together afresh

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: The thousand pounds I gathered has to count some cash meant as a subsidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' rearranges the three short words, and 'must include' puts old British slang for money inside. The grand is fodder, not a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A term for a sum given by central government to subsidise a body or project.

clue.text: Placed the wrong way, slates break

indicators.note: set down facing the wrong direction, so the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to slate is British usage for criticising harshly, as a critic pans a show

explanation.surface: Roof tiles laid incorrectly will crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Placed the wrong way' turns PANS round. To slate is British for criticising harshly, not a roofing tile here.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: something brittle will crack in two suddenly.

clue.text: Carp and egg served with cream

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a head louse
the cream of a group is its best part, the choice selection

explanation.surface: A fish dish and an egg dish both come with a creamy sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: None of the three foods is food: Carp is a verb meaning to find petty fault, the egg is a louse's, and the cream is the best of a bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to complain and find fault over trivial details.

clue.text: Join sailing vessel, something observable in the water

parts.note: as a noun, a join is the line where two pieces meet, as in sewing
Noah's vessel in Genesis

explanation.surface: Sign on with a ship's crew and you may spot something out among the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join' reads as a command but is a noun here, the line where two pieces of cloth meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a beacon or other conspicuous object visible from a ship and used for navigation.

clue.text: US state going into fish business — ultimately lots there?

indicators.note: going into means the state's abbreviation slots in between the fish and the final letter of business

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of business

parts.note: Ark is the traditional abbreviation of Arkansas

explanation.surface: An American state is moving into the fishing trade, where there is finally plenty to be had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' are American parking lots, which is why the state is American; 'going into' slots the state between the fish and the letter that 'ultimately' takes from business.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical American description: parking lots are what Britons call these places for leaving vehicles.

clue.text: Year on shop floor

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the year is added to the end of the shop

parts.note: a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Twelve months spent working among the staff of a retailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' tacks Y onto the end of STORE. The 'shop floor' phrase must be split: shop is wordplay, floor the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: one level of a building, in the British spelling.

clue.text: Creature slept upside-down, head tucked away

indicators.note: upside-down in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
the head, the top letter of the phrase, is put out of sight

parts.note: someone who slept briefly had (a) nap

explanation.surface: An animal dozed while hanging the wrong way up, with its head hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head tucked away' drops the H of HAD NAP, and 'upside-down' turns ADNAP round.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a black-and-white bear-like animal from China.

clue.text: A desert area in eastern French region

parts.note: to desert is to quit, to abandon a post
taken as written

explanation.surface: There is an arid tract in the east of part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is a verb, to abandon, not a stretch of sand, and 'in' is simply part of the spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic territory of south-west France, centred on Bordeaux.

clue.text: Mentioned form of punishment for murderer

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word for a punishment is heard rather than written

parts.note: the cane was the stick once used to beat schoolchildren

explanation.surface: Someone spoke of a kind of penalty fit for a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mentioned' signals that CANE is heard, giving a name with the same pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he killed his brother Abel, the first such crime in the Bible.

clue.text: Case of lady entering tube, heading for Earl's Court

indicators.note: entering means the two letters from lady go inside the word for tube

parts.note: a hose is a flexible tube

indicators.note: the case is the outer covering, so the first and last letters of lady
heading for picks the opening letter of Earl's

explanation.surface: A woman's suitcase is carried onto the Underground, bound for a west London station.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl's Court is a London Underground station; split it, and Court alone is the papal court. 'Case of', 'entering' and 'heading for' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal court: the government of the Roman Catholic Church at the Vatican.

clue.text: You briefly tucked into heavenly food one's served with last of cheese sauce

indicators.note: tucked into means the shortened word sits inside the word for heavenly food

parts.note: manna fell from heaven to feed the Israelites in Exodus

indicators.note: briefly tells you the word You loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened
the figure I for one, plus the letter S of the possessive

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of cheese

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed a divine dish that comes with the final scrap of a cheesy dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is the figure I plus S; 'briefly', 'tucked into' and 'last of' are the signals. The cheese only lends a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a thick cold dressing of egg yolks, oil and vinegar.

clue.text: Stone thrown in attack

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters are flung about into a new order

explanation.surface: A rock was hurled during an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' rearranges the letters of Stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a phrasal verb: to assault someone violently.

clue.text: Checks up on household, miles away in Hertfordshire town

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to vet something is to check it carefully

indicators.note: away means the letter for miles is taken out of the word for household

parts.note: a menage is a household

explanation.surface: Someone looks in on a family living some distance off in a town north of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is an English county just north of London. 'up' turns the checks, 'on' stacks the pieces and 'away' removes the miles.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a new town in the English county just north of London.

clue.text: Hikers disturbed songbird

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are unsettled from their order

explanation.surface: Walkers startled a small bird in full voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges the letters of Hikers.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a perching bird, also called the butcher bird, that impales its prey on thorns.

clue.text: Most unimpressive opera cycle left incomplete by a composer

parts.note: a pale imitation is an unimpressive one, so the most unimpressive is the palest

indicators.note: left incomplete means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Wagner's Ring is a cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: A musician abandoned their dullest set of operas before finishing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left incomplete' trims RING, Wagner's four-opera cycle, to RIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the sixteenth-century Italian master of church music.

clue.text: For example, during election broadcast, nothing standing out as worth watching

indicators.note: during means the abbreviation sits inside the rearranged letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are strewn into a new order
standing out means the letter for nothing stays outside and is not used

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: On polling-night television, say, not one item seemed worth tuning in for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing out' removes O from election, 'broadcast' rearranges the rest into TELENIC, and 'during' puts EG inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A description of someone who looks good on television.

clue.text: Back new cultural activities set up in Scottish port

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the whole run of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the back of something is its rear
the arts are cultural activities

explanation.surface: Support fresh arts projects being established in a harbour town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns the whole of REAR N ARTS upwards. The town is a ferry harbour in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a harbour town in Galloway, long the ferry terminal for Northern Ireland.

clue.text: City's financial institution agreed to accept grand

indicators.note: to accept means the pieces take the letter for grand inside them

parts.note: a bank is a financial institution
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
OK is said to show agreement

explanation.surface: A lender in London's financial district consented to take a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' suggests London's financial district but is just a capital; 'to accept' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the capital of Thailand.

clue.text: In the middle of the morning, i.e. when energy is fading

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, is the morning

indicators.note: is fading means the letter for energy disappears from the Latin phrase

parts.note: i.e. stands for the Latin id est, 'that is'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Halfway to noon is exactly the time when your get-up-and-go starts to flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is fading' drops E from ID EST, the Latin that i.e. abbreviates. The definition stops before 'the morning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a preposition: surrounded by, among.

clue.text: Sparkling wine, right, not still

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy

explanation.surface: A fizzy wine, certainly, and nothing flat about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' pretends to describe wine without bubbles; here it means motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: up and moving about, in motion.

clue.text: Chief petty officer initially having little room for manoeuvre?

indicators.note: initially means the officer's abbreviation comes at the start, before the word for chief

parts.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer
as an adjective, the chief point is the key one

explanation.surface: A senior naval rating at first found there was not much scope to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief' is an adjective meaning main, not part of a naval rank; 'initially' says the officer comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British adjective for a room that is uncomfortably small and cramped.

clue.text: Old man has little time for bygone days

parts.note: the old man is Pa, and 'Pa has' contracts to Pa's
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: An elderly gent is impatient with talk of yesteryear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man has' is PA'S, the contraction of 'Pa has', with T for time after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a noun: the time before now, history.
